# googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema (Data Source)

Chrome Policy Schema data source in the Terraform Googleworkspace provider. Chrome Policy Schema resides under the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chrome.management.policy` client scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

data "googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema" "example" {
  schema_name = "chrome.printers.AllowForUsers"
}

output "field_descriptions" {
  value = data.googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema.example.field_descriptions
}

# The full enum value names, by field.
output "enum_values" {
  value = {
    for f in data.googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema.example.enum_fields :
    f.field => [for v in f.values : v.value]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `schema_name` (String) The full qualified name of the policy schema

### Read-Only

- `access_restrictions` (List of String) Specific access restrictions related to this policy.
- `additional_target_key_names` (List of Object) Additional key names that will be used to identify the target of the policy value. When specifying a policyTargetKey, each of the additional keys specified here will have to be included in the additionalTargetKeys map. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--additional_target_key_names))
- `category_title` (String) Title of the category in which the setting belongs.
- `definition` (List of Object) Schema definition using proto descriptor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--definition))
- `enum_fields` (List of Object) The enum fields of the schema, also in nested messages, with the full names of their values. Use a value name as the value of the field in `googleworkspace_chrome_policy`. Confirm enum value names here instead of guessing a prefix. Each element has `field` (the field path, with a dot between the names of nested fields), `enum_type` (the fully qualified name of the enum type), and `values`. Each value has `value` (the full name), `number`, and `description` (from the known value in the field descriptions that is the full name, or else the longest known value that is the last part of the name after `_`; empty if there is none). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--enum_fields))
- `field_descriptions` (String) Detailed description of each field that is part of the schema, represented as a JSON string.
- `field_known_values` (List of Object) The known values of the fields of the schema, from the field descriptions, also for nested fields and for fields that are not enums. Each element has `field` (the field path, with a dot between the names of nested fields), `value`, and `description`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--field_known_values))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `notices` (List of Object) Special notice messages related to setting certain values in certain fields in the schema. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notices))
- `policy_api_lifecycle` (List of Object) The current lifecycle of the policy in the Chrome Policy API, empty if the API does not return it: `stage` (for example `API_CURRENT` or `API_DEPRECATED`), `description`, `end_support` (the date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, after which a change to a deprecated policy fails), `deprecated_in_favor_of` (the schema names of the policies that replace a deprecated policy), and `scheduled_to_deprecate_policies` (the schema names of the older policies that this policy replaces). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policy_api_lifecycle))
- `policy_description` (String) Description about the policy schema for user consumption.
- `support_uri` (String) URI to related support article for this schema.
- `supported_platforms` (List of String) The platforms on which the policy applies, for example `CHROME_OS` or `CHROME_BROWSER`.
